{
  "technical_and_design_decisions": [
    "Implement U1 as an in-process test harness using Spring application contexts and in-memory channels, avoiding external brokers while preserving module wiring, configuration properties, input, output, and assertion behavior.",
    "Use Spring Boot test support and the existing project messaging abstractions rather than introducing a separate testing framework; provide idiomatic assertions through the project's supported assertion libraries.",
    "Use the existing Spring Cloud Dataflow and Spring Cloud Stream extension points for binder, module, deployment, and admin-client changes wherever possible.",
    "Implement Redis Sentinel support through the existing Redis messaging/binder integration, using Sentinel-aware connection configuration and preserving compatibility with standalone Redis where practical.",
    "Treat the YARN work as an SPI investigation and working prototype rather than a production-hardened distributed scheduler implementation.",
    "Pass YARN definition parameters through the module deployment/container launch configuration and expose them to the running module using the established command-line or environment-property mechanism.",
    "Implement single-node binder auto-configuration using conditional Spring Boot auto-configuration, property binding, and dependency-based activation.",
    "Migrate the trigger module with minimal behavioral change, preserving its public configuration and stream-module conventions unless repository constraints require an adaptation.",
    "Upgrade receptor-client integration against the latest available Receptor API while isolating compatibility changes behind the existing client abstraction.",
    "Configure the existing admin UI client through server-side and client-side configuration changes rather than redesigning or replacing the UI.",
    "Include unit, integration, compatibility, and regression tests for each changed feature, with local/in-memory substitutes used where external infrastructure is not required.",
    "Use the project's existing Java, Spring, build, packaging, and continuous-integration conventions, targeting Java 17 or later where required by the Spring Framework baseline."
  ],
  "assumptions": [
    "The increment is implemented in an existing multi-module repository with established build, test, coding, and release conventions.",
    "Required Spring, Spring Cloud, Hadoop/YARN, Redis, Receptor, and admin UI dependencies are available or can be upgraded through normal dependency management.",
    "The specification does not require new product-level requirements, UX research, formal security certification, or production infrastructure provisioning.",
    "One developer performs analysis, implementation, testing, documentation, and integration work; estimates are work effort and exclude elapsed calendar time.",
    "U2 requires a documented investigation and executable YARN SPI prototype sufficient to derive a deployment strategy, not a complete production-grade YARN deployer.",
    "U4 assumes Redis Sentinel is used for high-availability Redis connectivity and that Redis server provisioning and operational monitoring are outside the increment.",
    "U6 assumes the existing admin UI client is functionally complete and needs compatible server and application configuration rather than substantial frontend feature development.",
    "U3 assumes the trigger module already exists in Spring XD and can be migrated without redesigning its business behavior.",
    "U5 assumes the latest Receptor API changes are available from documentation or source and that no major protocol rewrite is required.",
    "External-system testing for YARN, Redis Sentinel, and Receptor can use local containers, mocks, or test fixtures; access to a production cluster is not required.",
    "Documentation covers configuration, usage examples, limitations, and migration notes, but not a complete user manual."
  ],
  "activities": [
    {
      "activity_id": "A1",
      "activity_name": "Increment analysis and technical design",
      "activity_description": "Inspect the existing modules, extension points, build configuration, test conventions, and dependency versions; map U1-U8 to implementation locations; define interfaces, compatibility boundaries, configuration names, and test strategy.",
      "most_likely_effort": 6
    },
    {
      "activity_id": "A2",
      "activity_name": "In-process module integration-test support",
      "activity_description": "Build the test harness for module wiring and configuration-properties activation, support property combinations, provide in-memory input and output paths, add idiomatic assertions, and create representative module tests without requiring an external message bus.",
      "most_likely_effort": 15
    },
    {
      "activity_id": "A3",
      "activity_name": "YARN deployment SPI investigation and prototype",
      "activity_description": "Investigate YARN application and container lifecycle APIs, define the deployment SPI needed by the dataflow components, implement a working prototype for distributed module deployment, and document findings, limitations, and the recommended strategy for YARNModuleDeployer.",
      "most_likely_effort": 12
    },
    {
      "activity_id": "A4",
      "activity_name": "Trigger module migration from Spring XD",
      "activity_description": "Port the trigger source module into the Spring Cloud Stream repository, adapt package names and build metadata, align configuration and module descriptors with current conventions, and add source-level and pipeline-oriented tests.",
      "most_likely_effort": 8
    },
    {
      "activity_id": "A5",
      "activity_name": "Redis Sentinel message-bus support",
      "activity_description": "Add Sentinel-aware Redis connection and binder configuration, integrate it with stream and batch pipeline creation, preserve standalone Redis behavior where supported, and implement connection, failover-configuration, serialization, and end-to-end messaging tests.",
      "most_likely_effort": 15
    },
    {
      "activity_id": "A6",
      "activity_name": "Receptor client API upgrade",
      "activity_description": "Compare the current receptor-client integration with the latest Receptor API, update request and response models and invocation code, adapt error and status handling, and add compatibility tests for the changed API behavior.",
      "most_likely_effort": 8
    },
    {
      "activity_id": "A7",
      "activity_name": "Admin UI client server configuration support",
      "activity_description": "Update server-side configuration, endpoints, metadata, and compatibility settings required by the existing Spring Cloud Data admin UI client; verify login, discovery, resource access, and representative administrative workflows.",
      "most_likely_effort": 6
    },
    {
      "activity_id": "A8",
      "activity_name": "Single-node binder auto-configuration",
      "activity_description": "Create conditional auto-configuration for the single-node binder, bind and validate its properties, activate it based on classpath and application dependencies, define precedence and override behavior, and add positive, negative, and property-binding tests.",
      "most_likely_effort": 8
    },
    {
      "activity_id": "A9",
      "activity_name": "YARN definition-parameter propagation",
      "activity_description": "Add an option to carry stream or batch definition parameters into YARN container launch configuration, ensure safe escaping and serialization, expose the values to the module process through supported properties or arguments, and test propagation from definition through container execution.",
      "most_likely_effort": 8
    },
    {
      "activity_id": "A10",
      "activity_name": "Feature-specific automated testing",
      "activity_description": "Expand unit and integration coverage across the new test harness, trigger migration, Redis Sentinel support, Receptor changes, admin configuration, single-node auto-configuration, and YARN parameter handling; add mocks or containerized fixtures for unavailable external services.",
      "most_likely_effort": 12
    },
    {
      "activity_id": "A11",
      "activity_name": "Documentation and configuration examples",
      "activity_description": "Document new properties, test-harness usage, Redis Sentinel setup, YARN prototype and parameter behavior, single-node binder activation, Receptor compatibility, admin UI configuration, migration considerations, and example pipelines.",
      "most_likely_effort": 5
    },
    {
      "activity_id": "A12",
      "activity_name": "Build, packaging, and compatibility integration",
      "activity_description": "Update module descriptors, dependency management, generated metadata, packaging, release artifacts, and continuous-integration configuration; resolve cross-module compatibility issues and verify supported Java/Spring baselines.",
      "most_likely_effort": 6
    },
    {
      "activity_id": "A13",
      "activity_name": "End-to-end regression, defect correction, and delivery preparation",
      "activity_description": "Run the complete test suite and representative pipeline scenarios, exercise configuration combinations and failure paths, correct integration defects, perform final code cleanup, and prepare the increment for review and merge.",
      "most_likely_effort": 8
    }
  ],
  "reported_total": {
    "most_likely_effort": 117
  }
}

technical_and_design_decisions: Implement U1 as an in-process test harness using Spring application contexts and in-memory channels, avoiding external brokers while preserving module wiring, configuration properties, input, output, and assertion behavior.

Use Spring Boot test support and the existing project messaging abstractions rather than introducing a separate testing framework; provide idiomatic assertions through the project's supported assertion libraries.
Use the existing Spring Cloud Dataflow and Spring Cloud Stream extension points for binder, module, deployment, and admin-client changes wherever possible.

Implement Redis Sentinel support through the existing Redis messaging/binder integration, using Sentinel-aware connection configuration and preserving compatibility with standalone Redis where practical.
Treat the YARN work as an SPI investigation and working prototype rather than a production-hardened distributed scheduler implementation.

Pass YARN definition parameters through the module deployment/container launch configuration and expose them to the running module using the established command-line or environment-property mechanism.
Implement single-node binder auto-configuration using conditional Spring Boot auto-configuration, property binding, and dependency-based activation.
Migrate the trigger module with minimal behavioral change, preserving its public configuration and stream-module conventions unless repository constraints require an adaptation.
Upgrade receptor-client integration against the latest available Receptor API while isolating compatibility changes behind the existing client abstraction.
Configure the existing admin UI client through server-side and client-side configuration changes rather than redesigning or replacing the UI.
Include unit, integration, compatibility, and regression tests for each changed feature, with local/in-memory substitutes used where external infrastructure is not required.
Use the project's existing Java, Spring, build, packaging, and continuous-integration conventions, targeting Java 17 or later where required by the Spring Framework baseline.
assumptions: The increment is implemented in an existing multi-module repository with established build, test, coding, and release conventions.
Required Spring, Spring Cloud, Hadoop/YARN, Redis, Receptor, and admin UI dependencies are available or can be upgraded through normal dependency management.
The specification does not require new product-level requirements, UX research, formal security certification, or production infrastructure provisioning.
One developer performs analysis, implementation, testing, documentation, and integration work; estimates are work effort and exclude elapsed calendar time.
U2 requires a documented investigation and executable YARN SPI prototype sufficient to derive a deployment strategy, not a complete production-grade YARN deployer.
U4 assumes Redis Sentinel is used for high-availability Redis connectivity and that Redis server provisioning and operational monitoring are outside the increment.
U6 assumes the existing admin UI client is functionally complete and needs compatible server and application configuration rather than substantial frontend feature development.
U3 assumes the trigger module already exists in Spring XD and can be migrated without redesigning its business behavior.
U5 assumes the latest Receptor API changes are available from documentation or source and that no major protocol rewrite is required.
External-system testing for YARN, Redis Sentinel, and Receptor can use local containers, mocks, or test fixtures; access to a production cluster is not required.
Documentation covers configuration, usage examples, limitations, and migration notes, but not a complete user manual.
